title: Certify the residual two-cycle incidence class with full formal controls
body:
This scoped proof and finite certificate completes [JoyboyBrian's released connected-incidence handoff](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/6075#discussioncomment-19234840). It binds the predecessor two-write lemmas to a complete normalized incidence classification and full formal group-algebra controls. **No new κ, physical supplier or selected-frontier change is claimed.** The unrestricted five-coordinate ten- and eleven-call cases remain open.

The [proof and exact census domain](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/57b4c06ddd657c85823c8a11857cd5b54bb1837e/research/two-cycle-incidence-certificate/PROOF.md), [receipt](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/57b4c06ddd657c85823c8a11857cd5b54bb1837e/research/two-cycle-incidence-certificate/RESULT.json), [two-engine verifier](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/57b4c06ddd657c85823c8a11857cd5b54bb1837e/research/two-cycle-incidence-certificate/verify.py), and [source manifest](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/57b4c06ddd657c85823c8a11857cd5b54bb1837e/research/two-cycle-incidence-certificate/SOURCES.json) are pinned to `57b4c06ddd657c85823c8a11857cd5b54bb1837e`. Canonical base: `7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a`.

For the two-role target `[c]I`, with c a coordinate 3-cycle, pairwise-commuting rank-one projectors have exact cost twelve for every address dimension, including restored spectators. Each scalar lane needs six ordinary coordinate CNOTs. This completes the source application of credited methods; the ordinary lower bound, commuting reduction and handoff lemma are not claimed new.

At the ten-call residual, writer and reader pairs have equal projectors for spectators and complementary projectors for targets. A connected incidence graph therefore puts all projectors in one complementary pair and is excluded by the twelve-call bound. The complete finite classification is:

| Class | Normalized incidence assignments |
|---|---:|
| Inconsistent pair constraints | 5466 |
| Consistent connected graphs, excluded | 4992 |
| Disconnected graphs, unresolved | 3298 |
| Total | 13756 |

The remaining graphs admit 247,296 noncommuting projector assignments satisfying the pair equations. These are **not certified endpoints**. The census fixes writer pairs and enumerates loop-free reader assignments; relabeling call vertices forgets chronology. It is neither a chronological word search nor a graph-isomorphism census.

Validation on CPython 3.12.13, standard library:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/two-cycle-incidence-certificate
python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/two-cycle-incidence-certificate --check-source-history
```

Normal and optimized registered runs pass. Graph propagation agrees with independent GF2 elimination on every assignment; a separate counting dynamic program verifies the domain size. The ordinary BFS reaches exactly the independently enumerated 168 invertible 3x3 binary matrices. Matrix-label and complete-permutation-label engines agree on 36 twelve-call attainers, 216 lane-decomposition fixtures and all six versions of the connected handoff fixture. The latter fail the full endpoint despite passing pair constraints. All 432 single-call deletions fail. Controls detect wrong parity, omitted middle relabeling, an unfaithful natural quotient, noncommuting scope violations and all three changed predecessor files.

```text
PASS_TWO_CYCLE_INCIDENCE 13756 incidence assignments; 36 formal attainers; 432 deletion controls
PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/two-cycle-incidence-certificate outcome=completed
PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES
```

Metadata, ten committed package/input files, source ancestry and the official export's integrity/three-input coverage pass. The all-dimension proof reduces to the explicit finite GL3 base case; it does not extrapolate from sampled dimensions. The first [hosted run](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/41558037028) failed before package selection: the unchanged onboarding test read an empty `child-ready` file and raised `ValueError`. No package replay ran. GitHub denied a job retry because repository admin rights are required. Commit `c98e5b03` records this limitation; the new [hosted plan and package replay](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/41559592244) both pass at full head `c98e5b03a7d9001a155ba10bc9faad0ceb7cad68`. The scientific files at the links above are unchanged. No complete predecessor scientific suite, selected cold replay, unrestricted ten/eleven-call search, Lean, Docker, independent human review or proof-kernel verification ran.

Credit JoyboyBrian / @JoyboyBrian for [PR #6090](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6090) and the released incidence lemma, and Nick Petalas for [PR #6012](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6012). The consumed [two-write proof](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a/research/two-write-spectator-projection/README.md) and [all-dimension reduction](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a/research/two-three-cycles-every-dimension/PROOF.md) retain their exact bytes. Aaron Wang / @navinor supplied the earlier commuting reduction for a different SWAP target in [PR #2317](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2317), retained as [method context](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a/research/fiveswap-alt13-commuting-screen/README.md). James Reed / @jwr404 supplied [PR #5005](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5005) and [PR #5379](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5379); Mihir Srivastava supplied the formal model. The ordinary connectivity method retains Alan Bu, Evan Fan and Robert Joo's [primary-paper credit](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.07898).

Next: use the full selected-middle and off-subgroup equations on a bounded disconnected noncommuting pattern, preserving its actual chronology and `g b h` relabeling. No selected framework assumption is discharged. [Scoped coordination claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/6075#discussioncomment-19363628). Prepared by Ali Romman with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. New work is Apache-2.0.
